seo.title: Bali Summer Program | Pacific Discovery
seo.description: Bali in 4 weeks: food rescue and a mangrove clean-up in Sanur, Tabanan’s villages, surf camp in Uluwatu, service on Nusa Penida, a yoga retreat in Ubud and a Mount Batur sunrise. Ages 17–22.

hero.headline: Four weeks of service, surf and culture in Bali
hero.intro: Rescue food in Sanur, visit Tabanan’s villages and temples, learn to surf in Uluwatu, volunteer on Nusa Penida and finish with a yoga retreat and a sunrise on Mount Batur.

itinerary.heading: Week by week
itinerary.note: This is a guide to what you can expect to do on program. The order in which activities occur might vary. Itineraries are subject to change.

weeks.title: Sanur service & Tabanan villages
weeks.body:
You’ll meet your Program Instructors in Seminyak, where we spend a day on orientation before moving to the seaside town of Sanur. Here we join a mangrove clean-up, then help package meals with SOS, a food rescue organisation that turns good excess food from hotels and cafes into meals for people in need.

In Tabanan we stay at Coliving Bali and take meals out to local villages, visiting temples along the way. The next day brings trekking and cultural activities.
weeks.imageAlt: Students learning dance moves in an open-air pavilion

weeks.title: Tabanan Palace & surf camp
weeks.body:
A morning agriculture activity is followed by dinner at Tabanan Palace, the local royal palace built in 1343. Then we head to Uluwatu for surf camp with Balumba Surf School. Whether you’re a beginner or have surfed before, the instructors guide you through several days of lessons, with a restoration and exploration day in the middle.

At the end of the week we cross to Nusa Penida and settle in at FNPF, with activities on our first evening.
weeks.imageAlt: Group silhouetted on a leaning palm tree over the water at dusk

weeks.title: Nusa Penida service & Ubud culture
weeks.body:
We spend three days on a conservation service project with FNPF on Nusa Penida, then move to My Art Hostel for a free day to explore the island.

Back on the mainland, we settle into Ubud. A day with Five Pillars combines a cultural experience with a visit to an eco farm, and a batik making class follows.
weeks.imageAlt: Two people standing in a stone temple gateway reflected in water

weeks.title: Yoga retreat & Mount Batur sunrise
weeks.body:
After a morning at the markets, we head to Dragonfly Village for our yoga retreat with Sheila Ubud Yoga, starting with an orientation evening and continuing over the next three days.

After a final morning of yoga, we head to Mount Batur for a night in tents and a pre-dawn climb to the summit for sunrise. Back in Ubud we wrap up the program together before you fly home from Denpasar.

day.heading: What a typical day looks like

notes.title: Free time
notes.body: Each week there is some designated free time to catch up on email and laundry, rest and explore with others in the group.

notes.title: Phones & wifi
notes.body: We encourage flight mode so you stay present. Wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns.

notes.title: Fitness needed
notes.body: Medium activity level. Anyone with average fitness and enthusiasm for the outdoors will be fine. Expect several days of surf lessons, trekking in Tabanan, hands-on service projects and a pre-dawn climb up Mount Batur.

items.title: Food rescue in Sanur
items.body: Help SOS package meals made from good excess food rescued from hotels and cafes, then take meals out to villages in Tabanan.

items.title: Optional college credit
items.body: Earn college credit through the University of Montana. 529 education funds can be used to pay for your credits and your Pacific Discovery program tuition.

faq.heading: Questions we get about this program

items.q: Do I need to know how to surf?
items.a: No. The surf camp with Balumba Surf School in Uluwatu suits beginners as well as students who have surfed before.

items.q: How fit do I need to be?
items.a: Anyone with average fitness and enthusiasm for the outdoors will be fine. You don’t need experience with any of the activities, but be ready for surf lessons, trekking, service projects and a pre-dawn climb up Mount Batur.
Mostly hotels and hostels, plus Coliving Bali in Tabanan, a surf camp stay in Uluwatu, the FNPF centre on Nusa Penida, Dragonfly Village for the yoga retreat and one night in tents on Mount Batur.

items.q: What is the yoga retreat like?
items.a: A few days at Dragonfly Village in Ubud with Sheila Ubud Yoga, starting with an orientation evening, with yoga sessions each morning.

Tuition covers all in-country transport, accommodation, meals, and the activities and entry fees in the itinerary. It doesn't cover international flights, visas, travel insurance, spending money, optional college credit or optional activities.

items.q: How much spending money should I bring?
items.a: About $100 a week for snacks, laundry, personal shopping and optional activities. It varies from student to student.

items.q: Can I stay in touch with home?
items.a: Yes. We encourage keeping phones on flight mode so you stay present, and wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns. There will also be a photo album that students and instructors can upload photos and video to, so parents and caregivers can stay up to date.

items.q: Do I need a passport or visa?
items.a: Your passport must be valid for more than 6 months after the program ends. All the information you need in regard to visas will be available in your student portal.

safety.heading: For parents: how we keep students safe

items.title: 24/7 Emergency Line
items.body: Parents, students and instructors can reach a real person at any hour. Every call is logged and passed to our on-call staff member by phone.

items.title: Wilderness First Aid & Live Risk Assessment
items.body: All our instructors hold Wilderness First Aid (WFA) certification and have extensive training in group leadership and risk management.

items.title: Accredited Safety Systems
items.body: Our safety systems are assessed and accredited by the Gap Year Association (USA), Year Out Group (UK) and OutdoorsMark (NZ). Students on Go Overseas voted us one of the top gap year providers for safety.

items.title: Insurance & Health
items.body: Comprehensive travel insurance is required, covering medical costs and emergency evacuation. Check vaccinations with your doctor, and pack a first-aid kit and any personal medication. Our instructors can't legally give students any medication.
